plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the backpropagation computation graph for a neural network with four linear layers, laid out horizontally from left to right as a sequence of circles connected by arrows. The leftmost circle is labeled x_i (the input) and the rightmost is labeled ell_i (the scalar loss), with intermediate circles labeled with the upstream partial derivatives at each node: partial ell_i / partial f_0, partial ell_i / partial h_1, partial ell_i / partial f_1, partial ell_i / partial h_2, partial ell_i / partial f_2, partial ell_i / partial h_3, and partial ell_i / partial f_3, reflecting the chain-rule quantities accumulated during the backward pass. Each directed arrow between adjacent circles carries annotations below it for the local Jacobians needed to propagate gradients to the weights and biases of that layer, including partial f_k / partial omega_k and partial f_k / partial beta_k for k = 0 through 3; these branch off into separate annotations for the corresponding weight gradients partial ell_i / partial omega_k and partial ell_i / partial beta_k. All circles and arrows are rendered in black and white with thin strokes, giving the diagram a clean schematic appearance. This figure demonstrates the complete chain-rule decomposition used in backpropagation to compute gradients of the loss with respect to every weight and bias in a deep linear network.

interactionPlan.concept: Backpropagation computes the gradients ∂ℓ_i/∂β_k and ∂ℓ_i/∂ω_k by moving the loss gradient right-to-left through local derivatives, branching downward at each f_k node to form parameter gradients.

demo_steps.title: Source backward-gradient diagram
demo_steps.narration: The default view is the black-and-white backward-pass graph: arrows point right-to-left from ℓ_i, fraction derivative labels are visible, and every lower parameter-gradient branch is fully opaque.

demo_steps.title: Follow the chain rule backward
demo_steps.narration: Play the trace to see the gradient move from ∂ℓ_i/∂f_3 back through h_3, f_2, h_2, f_1, h_1, and f_0. The edge labels show the local derivative factor used at each step.

demo_steps.title: Branch to parameter gradients
demo_steps.narration: At each ∂ℓ_i/∂f_k node, the same backward signal branches downward to compute ∂ℓ_i/∂β_k and ∂ℓ_i/∂ω_k using the local derivative beside the diagonal branch.

demo_steps.title: Optional forward-pass explanation
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the forward-pass explanation only after reading the source diagram: the same chain is traversed left-to-right to compute f_0, h_1, f_1, h_2, f_2, h_3, f_3, and finally ℓ_i.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The backward graph is the chain rule drawn as reusable right-to-left gradients, with each f_k gradient splitting into the two parameter gradients for β_k and ω_k.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Default state must visually match the source textbook figure: monochrome only, white circular nodes with black outlines, black arrows pointing right-to-left, no blue forward arrows, no legend, no extra instructional coloring, and no hidden or faded lower branches. Render the diagram large enough for inline viewing: use oversized math labels inside circles and on edges, with fraction labels such as ∂ℓ_i/∂f_k, ∂ℓ_i/∂h_k, ∂ℓ_i/∂β_k, and ∂ℓ_i/∂ω_k comfortably readable. Place the main gradient chain in one horizontal row from ∂ℓ_i/∂f_0 at left through ∂ℓ_i/∂f_3 near the loss at right; place β_k and ω_k gradient circles below each f_k node with diagonal labeled arrows. Use the exact source notation consistently, especially the input notation x_i/𝓧_i, ℓ_i with script ell, β_k, ω_k, and the local derivative labels beside the diagonal parameter-gradient arrows. The forward-pass explanation is non-default and should not appear in the initial rendering; if shown, it should replace or lightly overlay the backward graph without adding a legend or default blue instructional styling.

plan.concept: Backpropagation computes every parameter gradient by propagating the loss gradient backward through a chain of local derivatives, branching at each layer to form weight and bias gradients.
elements: input circle labeled x_i at the far left
loss circle labeled ℓ_i at the far right
backward horizontal arrow from ℓ_i to ∂ℓ_i/∂f_3
forward-pass overlay labels f_0, h_1, f_1, h_2, f_2, h_3, f_3 aligned with the corresponding backward gradient nodes
forward-pass arrows from x_i through f_0, h_1, f_1, h_2, f_2, h_3, f_3 to ℓ_i
small legend indicating forward highlights and backward highlights

interactions.label: Computation direction
interactions.teaches: The network first computes activations from input to loss, but gradients are computed in the opposite direction from loss back toward earlier layers

interactions.label: Animate backward pass
interactions.teaches: Each gradient becomes available only after the gradient to its right has been computed, so backpropagation is a right-to-left chain-rule sweep with parameter-gradient branches at every layer
A selected gradient node depends on all upstream loss-to-node derivatives to its right, and each parameter gradient also multiplies by the local derivative for that layer's weight or bias

demo_steps.title: Forward computation
demo_steps.narration: In forward-pass mode, the input x_i is transformed through f_0, h_1, f_1, h_2, f_2, h_3, and f_3 to produce the scalar loss ℓ_i. The activations h_1, h_2, and h_3 are the intermediate values that later supply local derivatives during backpropagation.

demo_steps.title: Reverse the direction
demo_steps.narration: Switching to backward-pass mode replaces the forward values with gradient quantities such as ∂ℓ_i/∂f_3 and ∂ℓ_i/∂h_3. The arrows now point from the loss back toward earlier layers because the chain rule propagates sensitivity in reverse.

demo_steps.title: Sweep gradients backward
demo_steps.narration: Play the backward-pass animation: the highlight starts at ℓ_i, moves to ∂ℓ_i/∂f_3, then alternates through h-gradient and f-gradient nodes until it reaches ∂ℓ_i/∂f_0. This shows that each node's gradient is built from the already-computed gradient immediately downstream.

demo_steps.title: Branch to parameters
demo_steps.narration: At each f_k node, the backward signal branches downward to form ∂ℓ_i/∂β_k and ∂ℓ_i/∂ω_k by multiplying the upstream gradient by the local derivatives ∂f_k/∂β_k and ∂f_k/∂ω_k. Clicking a gradient node reveals exactly which chain of factors feeds it.

plan.keyInsight: Backpropagation is just the chain rule organized so one right-to-left pass reuses intermediate gradients to compute all weight and bias gradients efficiently.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Use a very wide horizontal black-and-white schematic matching the source: circular nodes with thin black outlines, math labels centered in each circle, and bold black arrows. Place x_i alone at far left and ℓ_i at far right; between them, arrange the gradient nodes in one top row alternating f-gradient and h-gradient labels, with arrows pointing left from the loss. Under each f-gradient node, draw two downward diagonal branch arrows to β and ω parameter-gradient circles, with the corresponding local derivative label beside each branch. In forward-pass mode, show the same positions as forward variables f_0, h_1, f_1, h_2, f_2, h_3, f_3 with arrows pointing right and emphasize h_1, h_2, h_3. Use subtle color only for interaction highlights, such as blue for forward activations, orange for active backward-chain nodes, and purple for selected parameter-gradient branches; keep the default diagram monochrome.
